problems.title: A common multiple must contain the lcm
problems.question: A positive integer is divisible by15 and20. Which listed number must also divide it?
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: $\operatorname{lcm}(15,20)=60$.
steps: The number is a multiple of60. Thus60 necessarily divides it. The other choices45,40,300 do not divide every multiple of60.

problems.title: Three consecutive angles of a cyclic quadrilateral
problems.question: Three consecutive angles of a cyclic quadrilateral have ratio4:3:6. Find its largest angle.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: Opposite cyclic angles sum to180°.
steps: Write the consecutive angles4t,3t,6t. Then4t+6t=180°,so t=18°.
The angles are72°,54°,108°,126°,and the largest is126°.

problems.title: A translated cube-root function
problems.question: Find the increasing interval of y=cube-root(x−2)+3.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: The real cube-root function is strictly increasing on all real numbers.
steps: Horizontal and vertical translations preserve this property. Thus the given function increases throughout its domain,which isℝ.

problems.title: Median and altitude to a right triangle’s hypotenuse
problems.question: A right triangle has hypotenuse median7;the angle between this median and the hypotenuse altitude is30°. Find the shorter leg.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: The hypotenuse is14. In the right triangle formed by the right-angle vertex,altitude foot and hypotenuse midpoint,h=7cos30°=7√3/2.
steps: If the legs areu≤v,thenu²+v²=14²=196 and uv=14h=49√3.
Hence(v²−u²)²=(u²+v²)²−4u²v²=9604,so v²−u²=98.
Subtracting gives2u²=98,so u=7.

problems.title: A shared-work rate
problems.question: The first worker alone needs8 days. Together the two workers need2 fewer days than the first alone. How long does the second need alone?
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: Together they need6 days;their rates satisfy $1/8+1/t=1/6$.
steps: The second rate is1/6−1/8=(4−3)/24=1/24 job per day.
Thus the second worker alone completes the job in24 days.

problems.title: An exponential inequality with a reciprocal input
problems.question: Solve2^(x/2)<4^(4/x).
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: Domain x≠0;equal base2 gives x/2<8/x,or(x²−16)/(2x)<0.
steps: The critical inputs are−4,0,4. A sign chart gives negativity on(−∞,−4) and(0,4).
The zeros−4,4 are excluded by strictness,and0 is undefined.

problems.title: Ratio of shifted exponential inputs
problems.question: For f(x)=8^(x+1),find f(x+2)/f(x−7).
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
steps: The input variable cancels. Convert to base2:8⁹=(2³)⁹=2²⁷.

problems.title: Add sine and cosine at fifteen degrees
problems.question: Evaluate sin15°+cos15°.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: $\sin t+\cos t=\sqrt2\cos(t-45^\circ)$.

problems.title: No positive solution to an exponential equation
problems.question: How many positive roots has3^x=sinx?
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: For x>0,3^x>1 while sinx≤1.
steps: The two sides cannot be equal for any positive input.

problems.title: A square root of a nonpositive square
problems.question: Find the range of f(x)=√(−cos²x).
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: Real square roots require−cos²x≥0,which is possible only when cosx=0.
steps: At every point of this nonempty domain,the function is0. Thus its range is the singleton{0}.

problems.title: A sum of cubes from tangent plus cotangent
problems.question: If tanα+cotα=b,find tan³α+cot³α.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: $u^3+v^3=(u+v)^3-3uv(u+v)$,and tanα·cotα=1.
steps: Substituting u+v=b gives b³−3b=b(b²−3).

problems.title: Combine logarithms after changing the base
problems.question: Evaluate log₄9+log₂(2√2/3).
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
steps: The logarithms of3 cancel,leaving3/2.

problems.title: An equilateral triangle in another triangle’s incircle
problems.question: A side-a equilateral triangle contains its incircle,and a regular triangle is inscribed in that circle. Find the smaller triangle’s side.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: The outer inradius is r=a√3/6. An equilateral triangle of circumradius r has side√3r.
steps: Thus the smaller side is√3·a√3/6=a/2.

problems.title: Count distinct roots of a factored equation
problems.question: For which a does(25^x−5)(x²−a²)=0 have exactly two distinct real roots?
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: The first factor gives x=1/2. The second gives x=±a.
steps: If a=0,the roots are0 and1/2. If a=±1/2,the roots are−1/2,1/2.
Every other a gives three distinct roots. Thus a∈{−1/2,0,1/2}.

problems.title: Which arithmetic-progression term lies in an interval?
problems.question: An arithmetic progression has a₂=4,a₆=14. Which listed term belongs to(20,40)?
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
steps: The interval condition gives20<2.5n−1<40,or8.4<n<16.4. Thus indices9 through16 qualify.
Of the listed indices12,14,16,18,the first three qualify;18 does not.
problems.answer: The12th,14th and16th listed terms all lie in(20,40).
problems.note: The question permits several listed answers. Their values are29,34,39;the18th value44 is outside.

problems.title: Two travellers and a returned walking stick
problems.question: A village and town are10.5km apart. A second walker leaves30min later at4km/h,meets the first,then returns a forgotten stick to the village. The first reaches town when the second returns. Find first speed.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: Let first speedu∈(0,4),meeting time t hours after the first departure. Thenut=4(t−1/2).
steps: Thus t=2/(4−u). The second returns distanceut at4km/h,so total elapsed time is t+ut/4.
The first’s arrival time gives10.5/u=t(1+u/4)=(4+u)/[2(4−u)].
Simplification givesu²+25u−84=0,whose positive root is3. The meeting occurs after2h;both final arrivals are at3.5h.

problems.title: Find which quadrants an even graph enters
problems.question: Which coordinate quadrants contain points of y=x²sin4−cos6,with angles in radians?
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: Here sin4 and cos6 are constants. Since π<4<3π/2,sin4<0;since3π/2<6<2π,cos6>0.
steps: The term x²sin4 is nonpositive for every real x. Subtracting the positive constant cos6 makes the entire function strictly negative.
For x<0 the graph lies in quadrantIII;for x>0 it lies in quadrantIV. At x=0 it lies on the negative y-axis.

problems.title: Sum of legs from area and hypotenuse
problems.question: A right triangle has hypotenuse25 and area150. Find the sum of its legs.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
steps: Then(u+v)²=625+600=1225. Since the lengths are positive,their sum is35.

problems.title: A dot-product condition selects a vector
problems.question: a=(1,2,3) and a·(a+b)=0. Which listed vector can b be?
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
steps: For b=(−19,1,1),the dot product is−19+2+3=−14. The other listed vectors give−1,−26,12,so they fail.

problems.title: Vector from a vertex to the centroid
problems.question: The medians of triangleABC meet atM. Express BM using BA and CA.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: $M=(A+B+C)/3$,so $\overrightarrow{BM}=(\overrightarrow{BA}+\overrightarrow{BC})/3$.
steps: Also BC=BA+AC=BA−CA. Therefore BM=(2/3)BA−(1/3)CA.

problems.title: Areas of two regular polygons in the same circle
problems.question: A regular octagon inscribed in a circle has areaQ. Find the area of a regular dodecagon inscribed in the same circle.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: A regular n-gon of circumradiusR has area$(n/2)R²\sin(2\pi/n)$.
steps: For n=8,the area is4R²sin45°=2√2R²=Q.
For n=12,the area is6R²sin30°=3R². The ratio is3/(2√2)=3√2/4.

problems.title: Circle inscribed in a one-hundred-twenty-degree sector
problems.question: A circle is inscribed in a120° sector of a radius-R circle. Find its circumference.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: If its radius isr,the centre’s distance from the sector vertex is d=r/sin60°=2r/√3. Internal tangency to the outer arc gives d+r=R.
steps: Solving givesr=√3R/(2+√3). Therefore its circumference is2πr=2√3πR/(2+√3).
problems.note: None of the displayed choices matches the120° sector calculation. The listed2πR/(2+√3) omits a factor√3.

problems.title: A decreasing logarithm reverses the comparison
problems.question: Solve log_(0.5)(x+2)≥1.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: Domain x>−2. Since0<0.5<1,the inequality is equivalent to x+2≤0.5.
steps: Combine x>−2 with x≤−1.5 to get(−2,−1.5].

problems.title: Projection length of a segment above a plane
problems.question: A length-125 segment has endpoints at distances100 and56 from a plane. Which listed length can its orthogonal projection have?
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: If endpoints are on the same side,the normal displacement is44;on opposite sides,it would be156>125,impossible.
steps: Thus the projection length is√(125²−44²)=√13689=117.

problems.title: A square prism diagonal inclined to a side face
problems.question: A regular quadrilateral prism has diagonal d=3√3,making angleα with a lateral face,with sinα=2/3. Find lateral surface area.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: For square-base sidea,height h,the diagonal satisfies d²=2a²+h². Its component perpendicular to a side face is a=d sinα.
steps: Lateral area=4ah=4·2√3·√3=24.

problems.title: Equal-edge regular hexagonal prism volume
problems.question: All edges of a regular hexagonal prism are equal. Its volume is12√3. Find its edge length.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: With edgea,the base area is(3√3/2)a² and heighta,so V=(3√3/2)a³.
steps: Set(3√3/2)a³=12√3. Then a³=8 and a=2.

problems.title: Area of a triangle formed by two projection feet
problems.question: An acute triangleABC has areaS. B₁,C₁ are the feet of altitudes fromB,C. If angleBAC=α,find areaAB₁C₁.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: $AB_1=AB\cos\alpha$ and $AC_1=AC\cos\alpha$. The angle between these two rays isα.
steps: Original area is(1/2)AB·AC·sinα. New area is(1/2)(ABcosα)(ACcosα)sinα.
Their ratio is cos²α,so the requested area isS cos²α.

problems.title: Areas on opposite sides of a trapezoid midline
problems.question: K lies on the midline segment of trapezoidABCD. Its area is18 and triangleABK has area2√3. Find areaCKD.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: K is halfway between the parallel bases. TrianglesAKD andBKC therefore have combined area half the trapezoid area.
steps: The other two trianglesABK andCKD account for the remaining half,9.
Thus areaCKD=9−2√3.

problems.title: A vector equation describes equal distances
problems.question: Given fixed pointsA,B in a plane,describe pointsX satisfying|AB+BX|=|BX|.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: Vector addition gives $\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BX}=\overrightarrow{AX}$.
steps: The equation becomes AX=BX. The locus of points equidistant from two distinct fixed points is the perpendicular bisector ofAB.
problems.note: This usual locus assumes A≠B. If the two fixed points coincide,every point of the plane satisfies the equation.

problems.title: Inradius-to-circumradius ratio in an isosceles triangle
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has base angleα. Find its inradius/circumradius ratio.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: $r/R=4\sin(A/2)\sin(B/2)\sin(C/2)$. Here A=B=α,C=π−2α.
steps: Thus r/R=4sin²(α/2)cosα.
Using sin2α=2sinαcosα and tan(α/2)=sinα/(1+cosα),this equals tan(α/2)sin2α,the listed form.

problems.title: Symmetry centres of bounded and unbounded figures
problems.question: A figure can have several or infinitely many symmetry axes. What is the maximum possible number of its symmetry centres?
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: Two central symmetries with different centres compose to a nonzero translation. A nonempty bounded figure cannot be invariant under such a translation.
steps: Thus a nonempty bounded figure has at most one centre.
However,the question does not require boundedness. An entire line has infinitely many symmetry centres:reflection through any point on the line preserves it. The whole plane is another example.
problems.answer: Without boundedness,infinitely many;for a nonempty bounded figure,at most1.
problems.note: The usual answer1 needs a bounded-figure condition. As printed,the “none of the previous answers” choice accommodates infinitely many centres.

problems.title: Distances between points in perpendicular planes
problems.question: Planesα,β meet orthogonally alongp. A∈α is distancea fromp,B∈β distanceb fromp,and their projections A₁,B₁ onto p are distancec apart. Find AB.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: Choose p as the x-axis,α as the xy-plane,β as the xz-plane. Then A=(u,±a,0),B=(v,0,±b),|u−v|=c.
steps: The squared coordinate distance is(u−v)²+a²+b²=c²+a²+b².

problems.title: Recover a homothety centre
problems.question: A homothety with k=−1/2 sendsA(1,2) toB(−3,4). Find its centreO.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
steps: Compute B+(1/2)A=(−5/2,5). Divide by3/2 to getO=(−5/3,10/3).

problems.title: A vanishing sum of vertex vectors
problems.question: In triangleABC,a pointM satisfies MA+MB+MC=0 as vectors. What is M?
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
steps: This is the coordinate formula for the centroid,the intersection of the medians.

problems.title: Cosine of a principal arctangent
problems.question: Evaluate cos(arctan(−3)).
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: The principal arctangent lies in(−π/2,π/2),where cosine is positive; $\cos^2t=1/(1+\tan^2t)$.

problems.title: Half-angle identity with the correct sign
problems.question: Simplify√(1+cos8),where8 is in radians.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: $1+\cos8=2\cos^24$,so its principal square root is√2|cos4|.
steps: Since π<4<3π/2,the cosine of4 is negative. Thus|cos4|=−cos4.

problems.title: A polynomial times a real cube root
problems.question: Solve(x²−4x+3)·cube-root(cosx)=0.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: The cube root is defined for every real cosx. The polynomial factors as(x−1)(x−3).
steps: The polynomial contributes x=1,3. The cube-root factor is zero when cosx=0,so x=π/2+nπ for every integer n.
All these inputs are valid;there is no nonnegative-radicand restriction for a cube root.

problems.title: A logarithm of a square needs an absolute value
problems.question: Solve log₃(x+2)+log₉((x−1)²)=1.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
steps: Combine logarithms to get(x+2)|x−1|=3.
For x>1,this becomes x²+x−5=0. Only(−1+√21)/2 is in that range.
For−2<x<1,it becomes x²+x+1=0,whose discriminant is negative. There are no additional roots.

problems.title: Angle between skew face diagonals of a prism
problems.question: A right prism has a right-triangle base with an acute30° angle. Its smallest lateral face is a square. Find the angle between nonintersecting diagonals of the other two lateral faces.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: Scale the short base leg and prism height to1. Use C=(0,0,0),A=(√3,0,0),B=(0,1,0),with top vertices one unit higher.
steps: The two larger lateral faces are overCA andAB. Take their skew diagonals A toC₁ and A₁ toB. Direction vectors areu=(−√3,0,1),v=(−√3,1,−1).
Their dot product is2,and lengths are2 and√5. Thus the smaller line angle has cosine2/(2√5)=1/√5.
The other nonintersecting diagonal pair gives the same absolute cosine.

problems.title: Two filling pipes with one switched off
problems.question: The first pipe fills a tank6h faster than the second. Both run5h;then the first is switched off and the tank finishes filling3h later. How long would the first need alone?
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: Let the first time be t>0,the secondt+6. Work fractions add to1:5/t+8/(t+6)=1.
steps: Multiplying gives5(t+6)+8t=t(t+6),or t²−7t−30=0.
This factors(t−10)(t+3)=0. The positive time is10h;the second time is16h.

problems.title: Count pairs of roots of a cosine-radical equation
problems.question: Find all a for which cos√(a²−x²)=1 has exactly8 real roots.
problems.idea: Keep the domain and all stated conditions while reducing the problem to a standard formula.
formulas: Let A=|a|. The radical takes values in[0,A];cos t=1 iff t=2πk,k=0,1,2,… . Each level below A gives two x-values;level A gives one.
steps: For A>0,the level0 contributes x=±A. Every positive level2πk<A contributes another pair.
To obtain exactly four pairs,the levels0,2π,4π,6π must lie below A and8π must lie above it. Thus6π<A<8π.
At A=6π or8π,a single x=0 is added at the endpoint level,so the root counts are7 or9 rather than8.
